newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: One of Cambodia's ruling parties forms new alliance.
newsitem.headline: One of Cambodia's ruling parties forms new alliance.

text.p: One of Cambodia's two ruling parties, the Cambodian People's Party (CPP), formed an alliance with a third group on Wednesday in what analysts saw as another step toward marshalling its forces ahead of polls due in 1998.

Cambodia's Second Prime Minister Hun Sen of the CPP and Information Minister Ieng Mouly, the head of a wing of the divided Buddhist Liberal Democratic Party (BLDP), signed the agreement at a ceremony attended by top officials.
"This is a faithful wedding, not a shotgun wedding," said Hun Sen.

Hun Sen on Monday signed a similar pact with the small Liberal Democratic Party, saying he expected alliances would be formed with up to 10 parties ahead of the local and general elections due by the end of 1998.

However, he said that the party was not trying to create a front to contest elections against the royalist FUNCINPEC party, with which the CPP currently shares power following U.N.-sponsored elections in 1993.
Ieng Mouly said the alliance would rather help to consolidate political stability and create an environment conducive to the holding of the next polls.

Analysts said the CPP moves were in response to plans by First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh to form an alliance between his FUNCINPEC party and pro-democratic forces, including the opposition Khmer Nation Party (KNP) and the other wing of the BLDP.
They said the two main coalition parties were clearly marshalling their forces ahead of the polls and warned that such alliances could exacerbate their strained relations.

Ties between the two have deteriorated due to FUNCINPEC demands for more power to reflect their narrow victory in the 1993 elections and separate efforts by both premiers to win the allegiance of thousands of defectors from the rebel Khmer Rouge guerrilla faction.
